GPUs are getting faster every year.

But memory bandwidth? Barely keeping up.

This is the "memory wall" — and it's the real bottleneck for AI.

Here's what's happening (thread)

The fix isn't just "more memory."

Researchers found that reorganizing how data flows — KV Cache compression + sparse attention — cuts memory use by 60%.

Same accuracy. 2x throughput.

Why this matters for the industry:

- Smaller models can now rival larger ones
- Inference costs drop significantly
- Edge deployment becomes viable

The bottleneck is shifting from compute to architecture.

The future of AI isn't just bigger models.

It's smarter memory.
